correctness.rationale: For the ordinary Lovász Hom(C5,K4) complex, every nontrivial D5 element has no invariant cell: 5-cycle rotations force five equal adjacent-disjoint nonempty colour sets, and each pentagon reflection exchanges endpoints of an edge. Thus the degree-ten orbit projection is a regular covering. Published Csorba–Lutz identifies the covering manifold as SO(3)=RP3; the Dover–Özaydın single-reflection equivariance identifies the involution with a right multiplication by a pi rotation of SO(3), whose lift in SU(2) has order four and square the central deck involution. The order-twenty central extension is C5 ⋊ C4 with inversion action, equivalently Dic5. Reflection orientation preservation extends to D5, so Poincare duality and abelianization give integral H=(Z,Z/4,0,Z). Independent exhaustive integer cellular reconstruction from actual cell rule: 2,160 source cells, orbit degrees (24,78,84,30), d1,d2,d3 Smith invariant factors 1^23;1^54,4;1^29, with d²=0. The SNF checks H1 but not alone the nonabelian π1.
